texts.preamble: Jagdish Shah (Dar) vs Sushil Kumar Chatuvedi (21/21,Dc on 21 March, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No: 550/2021 Jagdish Shah vs. Sushil & ors. Cnr No: Dlse01-0081232021 1. Jagdish Shah S/o Nathni Shah R/o House no. 1795, Gali no.3, Surya Colony Sehatpur, Amarnagar, Faridabad, Haryana 121003. .....Petitioner Versus 1. Sushil Kumar S/o Sh. Ram Kishor R/o Village-Bati, Ps Kauthal Distt. Dausa Rajasthan. ............Driver/Respondent no.1 2. M/s Lucky Transport Company Sh. Parminder Singh R/o 122 Dhobiana Basti Distt. Bathinda, Punjab Mact No.550/21 Jagdish Shah vs. Sushil Kumar & ors. P.No. 1 of 21 ss Charu Gupta Gupta 2025.03.21 16:16:01 +0530 ............Owner/Respondent no.2 3. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Office at: 8th Floor, Kanchan Jhanga Building, 18, Barakhamba, Road New Delhi ......Insurance Company/Respondent no.3 Date of accident : 11.02.2021 Result of accident : Injury/permanent disability Date of filing of Dar : 21.09.2021 Date of Decision : 21.03.2025 Award 1. The present DAR arises out of road accident that occurred on 11.02.2021, in which the petitioner Jagdish Shah allegedly suffered grievous injury.
texts.facts: An FIR no. 21/2021, dated 11.02.2021 was registered u/s 279/338 of IPC against respondent no.1 (driver of the offending vehicle). The offending bus was seized on the same day from the spot and driver of the offending vehicle was arrested. Upon investigation a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court and a claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver, respondent no.2 is owner of the offending vehicle and respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured. 5. Despite opportunity none of the respondents filed any reply to the claim of the petitioners. On 25.07.2023 following issues were framed: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 11.02.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. RJ-09PA-4728 (bus) driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3 ? OPP. 3. Relief. 6. Thereafter, evidence was led by the petitioner by examining himself as PW-1. PW-1/petitioner Jagdish Shah tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated the contents of the DAR and relied upon documents i.e. Medical bills which is Ex.PW1/1 (colly), FIR dated 15.02.2021 as Ex.PW1/2, DAR as Ex.PW1/3, copy of Adhar card as Ex.PW1/4 (OSR) and certified of disability as Ex.PW1/5. PW-1 was duly cross examined by counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
